messages:
Alex: Quick sync — we need a clear decision on egress affinity semantics for private endpoints. Customer wants source IP preserved across control-plane failovers. Is that doable without per-tenant NAT?
Nora: Short answer: preserving exact client source IP across CP failover is hard if we use shared egress. Options are per-tenant SNAT, sticky egress anchors, or accepting IP rotation (documented).
Sanjay: Alternatives to consider: 1) per-tenant egress ENIs (dedicated IPs) 2) ephemeral sticky relay that follows sessions 3) DNAT rotation + graceful retries. Tradeoffs on cost/complexity.
Liz: For Dedicated customers ENIs make sense. For Hosted it's too expensive at scale. We need a middle product.
Maya: Middle ground idea: small ephemeral pool reserved per-tenant, leased for session TTLs. Cheaper than full ENI but gives IP stability during short failovers.
Alex: @Nora can you sketch failure modes? Specifically if CP failover moves control to another region, what actually breaks for customer backends?
Nora: When CP failover causes traffic to egress from a different relay, the observed source IP changes. TCP connections drop. Some customer infra rely on IP allowlists so they see a new IP and reject.
Sanjay: Implementation option: 'sticky egress' map in dataplane with lease TTL. During handoff, relay A streams lease bundle to relay B, B imports leases and takes over NAT flows. Complexity: KV sync + race windows.
Liz: Syncing leases introduces replication lag. If a client reconnects before migration completes, they might get a different IP — which defeats the goal.
Maya: What about a targeted handoff API between relays instead of global CP sync? e.g. `POST /handoff` sending a compact lease bundle for specific tenants/sessions.
Alex: How does that differ between peering (route-based) and private endpoint models?
Nora: With VPC peering the relay can live in customer VPC and keep the original source IP (no SNAT). With private endpoint (our VPC) we must NAT at our edge, so we need stable public IPs or managed pools to preserve identity.
Sanjay: For private endpoint customers we can productize an "ephemeral-static" option: reserve a tiny pool of stable egress IPs per tenant. Billable add-on. Lower cost than full ENI but gives predictable IPs.
Liz: Action items: Nora to write a short RFC for the relay-handoff API + lease format. Maya to run cost model for ephemeral-static pools. Alex to update customer onboarding checklist and FAQ.
Nora: I'll draft the RFC today. Working title: "relay handoff API and egress lease format". Draft link (WIP): https://go/reviews/egress-handoff :writing_hand:
Maya: +1 on draft. @deploy-bot can you kick off a smoke test that validates lease handoff behavior between two staging relays?
deploy-bot: deploy queued: egress-handoff-smoke-tests -> staging (eta ~12m) :rocket:
Alex: Sounds good. If anyone has a strong objection to the sticky-egress + billable pool approach, speak now. Otherwise we'll align on RFC and offer the pool as a Private endpoint upgrade. :thumbsup:
Liz: +1
Sanjay: +1
Maya: +1
